scope: October 13, 2025 Law: common rules, Standard Setup, Marquise de Cat, Eyrie Dynasties, Woodland Alliance, one Vagabond, Fall/Autumn and Winter maps, core dominance/coalitions, Thief/Tinker/Ranger. Excludes other factions/characters, second Vagabond, hirelings, landmarks, bots and Advanced Setup.
method: Read the complete relevant extracted rules (chapters 1–9 excluding 9.7, C.1, Appendix G, M.1–2 and V.1–3) and the entire summary. Cross-checked the Revolt, piece-manipulation, building-slot, map and base-character passages directly against text extracted from the authoritative PDF. Did not consult questions, answer keys, reader answers, grades or other QA files. No outside sources used.

findings.issue: The Revolt paragraph adds an open-building-slot prerequisite to taking Revolt. The Law requires a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base on the Alliance board, and payment of two matching supporters. Base placement is part of resolving the effect, not a listed prerequisite.

source_refs.evidence: Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base on your faction board; spend two matching supporters; remove enemy pieces, then place the base, warriors and officer.
If prompted to place pieces but unable to do so fully, place the maximum possible; this does not waive costs or prerequisites.
A building cannot be placed in a clearing with no open slots.

findings.impact: A reader may incorrectly disallow an otherwise legal Revolt when no base slot can be opened. Resolve removal first, then place as much as possible; inability to place the base does not cancel the other Revolt effects. The current sentence may also be read as requiring the slot before removing enemy buildings.
findings.suggested_correction: Delete the added prerequisite. If a slot clarification is desired, state that base placement requires an open slot after enemy removal, and otherwise follow the maximum-possible piece-placement rule.
